summary: Lists requirements for the mechanisms that dynamically move the resources of a switching element, such as an ATM switch, between its partitions. This matters when an operator leases control of a partition to a third party. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A big switch can be cut into parts and each part rented to a different company. This memo lists what is needed to resize those parts while the switch keeps running.

questions: how do you resize a switch partition while it is running
what are the requirements for dynamic partitioning
subtitle: Requirements for reshaping switching element resources without stopping the service.

tldr.problem: When an operator leases parts of a physical network switch to different customers, static repartitioning requires shutting down partitions, losing state and causing downtime. Operators want to add or remove resources dynamically while the switch is running.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines 17 requirements for dynamic partitioning, covering resource creation, notification of changes, handling resource requests, security controls and tools to determine what resources are available and how they are allocated.
tldr.outcome: Switching element manufacturers and operators now have a blueprint for systems that can resize virtual switches while they are in use, reducing service interruptions and operational costs when reallocating infrastructure.

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: Informational; intended for GSMP switches and forwarding elements

facts.label: Primary use case
facts.value: Operator leasing partitions to multiple tenants

today: RFC 3532 is an Informational RFC that remains relevant for operators deploying multi-tenant network infrastructure. It codified requirements that informed later work on network slicing and infrastructure virtualization, though it was never mandatory.

sections.title: Key concepts: partitions, controllers and managers
sections.content:
A switching element (SE) is a network device like an ATM switch that forwards packets. A partition is a set of the switch's resources (ports, memory, processing capacity) that can be controlled independently. A controller is the software that manages one or more partitions and directs how they forward traffic. A partition manager (PM) is the administrative software that decides how to divide the switch's resources and allocates them to partitions.

In static partitioning, changing the resources of an active partition requires disconnecting its controller and restarting the partition. In dynamic partitioning, resources can be reallocated without stopping the partition. A frozen partition is one that is being shut down: it keeps serving existing connections but does not accept new ones, and its unused resources are returned to the switch.
sections.eli5: A switch is divided into pieces called partitions. A partition manager runs the whole switch, and controllers manage individual partitions. Dynamic partitioning means resizing the pieces while they are running.

sections.title: The problem with static repartitioning
sections.content:
Static repartitioning is costly. Before reallocating resources, all controller connections to the affected partitions must be severed, the state they configured is lost, and the partition is placed in the down state during repartitioning. Afterwards, controllers must reconnect and reestablish state, causing a period of downtime and lost service.

Dynamic partitioning avoids this downtime by allowing resources to be shifted without disconnecting controllers or losing state. However, new challenges arise: how is a controller notified that its resources have changed? What happens if the partition manager wants to take back resources that are currently in use?
sections.eli5: The old way of resizing a partition meant turning it off, moving resources around, and turning it back on. New way: do it while it is running, but now you need new rules for how that works.

sections.title: Resource creation and enforcement
sections.content:
The RFC requires that a partition manager MUST be able to create virtual SEs and allocate resources to them. The switch MUST prevent controllers from using more resources than are currently allocated to their partition, enforcing limits by rejecting requests that exceed available resources with either an explicit error code (reactive notification) or a generic error (implicit reactive notification).

Importantly, the switch MUST guarantee that all resources discoverable through the GSMP protocol can be partitioned. Resources used indirectly (such as CPU, forwarding table entries) MAY be partitioned but are not required to be.
sections.eli5: The manager can create new virtual switches and say how many ports each one gets. The real switch has to say no if a controller asks for more than it is allowed.

sections.title: Denial and escalation mechanisms
sections.content:
If a partition manager asks the switch to take back resources that are currently in use by a controller, the switch MUST deny the request. This prevents data loss but could cause the manager to be unable to reallocate resources if a controller is uncooperative.

To handle this, the RFC gives the partition manager three escalation tools. First, it SHOULD be able to freeze a partition, which stops it from accepting new connections and returns unused resources. Second, it SHOULD be able to ask the controller to voluntarily reduce its resource usage. Third, the manager MUST be able to exercise power-on/off control: turning off a partition's virtual power disconnects all controllers and forces them to reinitialize, allowing the manager to fall back to static partitioning if necessary.
sections.eli5: If a controller is holding resources it does not need, the manager can ask nicely, or freeze the partition to stop new work, or force it offline if that does not work.

sections.title: How changes are communicated
sections.content:
The RFC allows multiple ways for a controller to learn that its resources have changed. Control protocols MAY include proactive resource notifications, where the switch tells the controller immediately when resources change. The switch MAY inform the partition manager of resource exhaustion on a particular partition so the manager can intervene. The partition manager MAY directly contact a controller to inform it of resource changes rather than relying on the switch to do so. Controllers MAY also ask the partition manager for more resources or for permission to reduce their usage.

To support automation, the partition manager MUST be able to query the switch to discover which controllers are attached to a partition and what control protocol each is using. This allows the manager to contact controllers programmatically.
sections.eli5: The switch can tell a controller its resources changed, or the manager can tell the controller, or the controller can ask. The manager needs to know which controllers to contact.

sections.title: Security of the partitioning system
sections.content:
Only authorized partition managers may dynamically repartition a switch. The switch MUST use a secure process to determine which partition manager controls it, either by explicit specification or by using a discovery protocol. Only the authorized partition manager (or an authorized agent) may contact controllers to request they reduce resource usage or inform them of resource changes.

The partition manager MUST verify and authenticate that any requests for additional or fewer resources have come from a controller that is authorized to control the specified partition. Failure to do so could allow an attacker to cause a controller to release resources or consume them maliciously.
sections.eli5: Only a trusted manager can reshape the switch, and only trusted controllers can ask for resource changes. Everyone has to prove who they are.
